name: Beti (Cameroon)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Retired ISO code btb: Glottolog marks Beti (Cameroon) as a group name, not a language (split 2010-01-18 per CR 2009-032); only bookkeeping references exist

sources.citation: von Hagen, Gunther Tronje. 1914. Lehrbuch der Bulu-Sprache. Berlin: Radetzki. vii+402 pp. — §7 'Betonung und Tonlehre', pp. 13-14 (per DNB table of contents held under bulu1251).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Member language Bulu (bulu1251) is the one large Beti-group language with no opened stress statement; the TOC shows a section titled 'Betonung' that would carry it. HathiTrust uc1.b4017012 is full view (pdus) but could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Nekes, P. Hermann. 1911. Lehrbuch der Jaunde-Sprache. (Lehrbücher des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin 26.) Berlin: Georg Reimer. §19 'Der dynamische Akzent', p. 26.
sources.note: For Ewondo/Jaunde (ewon1239, the core 'Beti' variety; Glottolog beti1249 'Beti' is a dialect of it), not for the group: §19 'In der Regel ist die erste Stammsilbe akzentuiert. Die übrigen Silben sind oft so schwach akzentuiert, daß ihre Vokale..' (the scanned text); §15 says the dynamic accent is independent of tone. Already the basis of the ewon1239 catalog entry (reading morphologically determined), together with Heepe 1919 p. 152.

sources.citation: Bates, George Latimer. 1904. Handbook of Bulu, with a Bulu-English vocabulary. Elat, Kamerun: Presbyterian Mission (2nd ed. 1926, with Silas F. Johnson).
sources.note: Primary Bulu description cited by Alexandre & Binet for its tone analysis; its phonetic introduction (pp. 4-8) is the other likely carrier of a Bulu accent statement. HathiTrust wu.89097901672 is public-domain full view but could not be reached by automated download.
sources.venue: Elat, Kamerun: Presbyterian Mission (2nd ed. 1926, with Silas F

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change Request Number 2009-032: retire [btb] Beti (Cameroon) (submitted by John E. McLaughlin, Utah State University, 2009-06-12; adopted 2010-01-18). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Not a description. p.2 §3(b): 'Beti is actually a group name, not a language name. Language group members are Bebele [beb], Bebil [bxp], Bulu [bum], Eton [eto], Ewondo [ewo], Fang [fan], and Mengisa [mct], all of which already have their own code elements.' §3(c) cites Ethnologue 15 ('partially intelligible but ethnically distinct') and Maho 2003 (Beti not listed as a language in A.70). Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Alexandre, Pierre & Jacques Binet. 1958. Le groupe dit Pahouin (Fang – Boulou – Beti). (Monographies ethnologiques africaines, IAI.) Paris: Presses Universitaires de France. vi+152 pp. HRAF microfiche scanned (FH9 Fang file 019).
sources.note: Chapter 'La langue' (by Alexandre), phonetic remarks (the scanned text): 'Au point de vue phonétique, la caractéristique la plus importante du groupe est sans doute l'emploi de tons..'; contrasts Bates & Johnson (five tones + negative glissando), Bertaut/German authors (H, L, rising, falling, mid) and Stoll; says rhythm matters as much as tone in drum language. No statement whatsoever on stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/intensité: only orthographic 'accent circonflexe').
sources.venue: (Monographies ethnologiques africaines, IAI.) Paris: Presses Universitaires de France. vi+152 pp

sources.citation: Van de Velde, Mark L.O. 2008. A Grammar of Eton. (Mouton Grammar Library 46.) Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter. Ch. 2 Phonology, §'Accent'.

sources.note: Published version of the Eton statement already quoted in the eton1253 check from the 2006 Leuven thesis; a citation upgrade only.

sources.citation: Essono, Jean-Marie. 2000. L'ewondo, langue bantu du Cameroun: phonologie, morphologie, syntaxe. Yaoundé: Presses de l'UCAC / ACCT. (Thesis version: Essono 1993, Paris III, 1994PA030076.)

sources.note: Modern reference grammar of Ewondo, the central 'Beti' variety (Glottolog beti1249 'Beti' = dialect of ewon1239); would supersede the 1911-1919 German sources on which the ewon1239 stem-initial-accent statement rests.

sources.citation: Abessolo Nnomo, Thierry. 1981. Essai de tonologie de la langue beti: le ton grammatical dans le syntagme nominal. Mémoire, Université de Yaoundé I. 68 pp.

sources.note: The only work in Glottolog's bibliography that treats 'la langue beti' phonologically under that name; a tonology of the noun phrase may state whether an accent exists alongside tone. Not held by BnF/SUDOC; Yaoundé print only.

sources.note: No language work titled 'Beti' on archive.org. Hits are the member-language grammars already held in sibling check dirs: Nekes 1911 & 1913, Heepe 1919, Redden 1979, Pichon 1950 (ewon1239); Largeau 1901, Ndongo Esono 1956 (fang1246). Bates 1904/1926 and von Hagen 1914 (Bulu) are not on archive.org.

sources.citation: BnF catalogue général, SRU API: subject 'Beti (langue)' (26 records) and title 'beti' + subject 'langue' (22 records), queried 2026-09-17.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: No grammar or phonology of a language called 'Beti' is held by the BnF. Only language-tagged items: Amayina, Patrice 2014 'Le kolo beti, ewondo' (146 p.) and 2016 'Fek beti be koba: le savoir des antiques philosophes' (306 p., subject Beti (langue)) — proverb/philosophy books; Tsala/Vincent/Bouquiaux 1986 'Mille et un proverbes beti' (subject Ewondo (langue)). All other hits concern the novelist Mongo Beti.

The other seven are literary theses on Mongo Beti.
